newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt yields inch up, focus on Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt yields inch up, focus on Greenspan.

text.p: 1550 GMT - Swedish debt yields ended the session on Wednesday off the day's highs, closing a touch higher while the crown firmed.
The main influence was weaker foreign markets, but technical factors also played their part, one dealer said.
* Six-month T-bill rates rose two basis points to 4.23 pct
* The ten-year bond yields climbed one basis point to 6.86 pct
* The crown firmed to 4.4640 against the mark from 4.4720

Swedish debt yields rose slightly across the curve on Wednesday driven by weaker foreign markets. The debt market mirrored the curency market which has been rather volatile but Sweden fared better than Germany.

"We've decreased the spread since we've had technical levels as ceilings. That has prevented the Swedish debt yields climbing as much as the German, but has, at the same time, allowed them to back down when the German's did," one dealer said.
Six-month T-bill rates were up two basis points at 4.23 percent and the ten-year bond yields rose one basis point to 6.86 percent, but were higher most of the day.
Meanwhile the spread between Swedish and German long debt yields decreased seven basis points to 119.
The crown firmed to 4.4640 against the mark compared to 4.4720 late on Tuesday.
During the day it peaked at 4.800.
"There has been lot of speculations but at the end of the day we must have seen some export flows", one dealer said.
